methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
RISE Robotics, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Arron Acosta and Blake Sessions, has raised $22M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company in the robotics sector, spanning seed through Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $22M total raised as a base proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implying a $44M valuation. Peer-median analysis references a cohort of 4 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed)—yielding a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $37M (low), $872M (median), and $2.0B (high). The stage-progression floor reflects mechanistic application to current funding; the peer median sits substantially higher, reflecting later-stage comparables in the dataset. Key uncertainties include the composition of the peer set (weighted toward Series B), the relevance of the stage-progression multiplier absent visibility into revenue or growth metrics, and the extent to which public and private robotics valuations reflect durable fundamentals versus sector-specific sentiment. A narrower range would require revenue, unit economics, or customer traction data.
